hits.text: In 2023, on a non-GAAP basis excluding the impact of direct costs resulting from the Incident, income from railway operations decreased due to lower railway operating revenues and higher railway operating expenses. Railway operating revenues declined due to decreased fuel surcharge revenue, decreased intermodal storage revenues, and lower volume, partially offset by increased pricing and favorable mix compared to the prior year. Railway operating expenses increased due to inflationary pressures, investments in operational resiliency, and higher service-related costs, partially offset by lower fuel prices.
hits.section: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

hits.text: On an adjusted basis, income from railway operations in 2024 increased due to lower adjusted railway operating expenses, with lower fuel prices, decreased costs of purchased services, and lower other expenses contributing significantly to the overall decline, and more than offsetting the decline in revenue. Lower other income-net and higher interest expense on debt contributed to net income and diluted earnings per share that were only up slightly compared to the prior year.
hits.section: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

hits.text: Metals and construction revenues were higher in 2024 but lower in 2023 compared with the prior years. In 2024, the increase was driven by higher average revenue per unit due to favorable price, partially offset by lower fuel surcharge revenue, and higher volume. Increased volume was due to higher demand in aggregates, kaolin, miscellaneous construction, and scrap metal, partially offset by lower demand for coil steel shipments. In 2023, the decline in revenue was driven by lower average revenue per unit, the result of decreased fuel surcharge revenue partially offset by increased price. Volumes were nearly unchanged as reduced shipments of kaolin and construction materials were offset by volume gains in coil steel and scrap metal. The volume declines in kaolin were largely driven by lower demand, while the declines in construction materials were due to lower demand, extended cycle times and service challenges. Gains in coil steel volume were due to increased equipment available to handle demand, while scrap metal volume increased due to higher demand.
hits.section: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

hits.text: non-Incident-related railway operating expenses. Railway operating revenues declined 5% due to lower average revenue per unit, the result of lower fuel surcharge revenue and decreased intermodal storage service revenues partially offset by favorable pricing and mix. Additionally, lower volumes contributed to the decline in revenues. Net expenses associated with the Incident for the year 2023 were $1.1 billion. In addition to costs resulting from the Incident, railway operating expenses increased due to inflationary pressures, investments in operational resiliency, and higher service-related costs, offset partially by lower fuel prices. The decline in net income and diluted earnings per share also reflects the absence of a prior year $136 million deferred tax benefit, a result of an enactment of a change in the corporate income tax rate in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania in 2022. Railway operating ratio deteriorated to 76.5 percent.
hits.section: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

hits.text: Materials expense increased in both 2024 and 2023. The increase in 2024 was due to higher freight car repairs expense, partially offset by lower locomotive materials spending. The increase in 2023 was due to increased locomotive, freight car, and track materials costs.
hits.section: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

hits.text: In 2024, the decline in railway operating expenses reflects lower net expenses related to the Eastern Ohio incident (Note 18), higher gains on operating property sales, including certain gains on railway line sales (Note 8), and lower fuel prices, partially offset by restructuring and other charges (Note 3), and increased depreciation on our higher asset base. In 2023, expenses increased as we incurred $1.1 billion of costs related to environmental matters and legal proceedings resulting from the Incident (Note 18). Additionally, railway operating expenses reflected higher costs due to inflationary pressures, investments in operational resiliency, and higher service-related costs. Partially offsetting these increases were the impacts of lower fuel prices and the absence of retroactive wage increases recorded in 2022.

message.content: I have strong evidence. Let me compute the reported margins and the operating ratio change.

Norfolk Southern's overall profitability margins improved sharply in fiscal 2024 (year ended 31 Dec 2024) versus fiscal 2023, driven mainly by lower operating expenses rather than revenue growth.

**Reported margins (derived from XBRL facts, USD)**

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Railway operating revenues | $12,156M | $12,123M | −0.3% |
| Income from railway operations (operating income) | $2,851M | $4,071M | +42.8% |
| Operating margin (operating income / revenue) | 23.5% | 33.6% | +10.1 pts |
| Pretax income | $2,320M | $3,329M | +43.5% |
| Net income | $1,827M | $2,622M | +43.5% |
| Net margin (net income / revenue) | 15.0% | 21.6% | +6.6 pts |

Sources: revenue fact IDs 859727 (FY2023) and 859736 (FY2024); operating income 855250 and 855259; pretax income 850745 and 850754; net income 854469 and 854482 — all from the FY2024 10-K, accession 0000702165-25-000008, filed 2025-02-10. FY2023 figures are identical to those originally filed in the FY2023 10-K (accession 0000702165-24-000005, filed 2024-02-05), so no revision issue arises. Margins are my calculations, not disclosed fields.

**What drove the change (management's explanation, FY2024 10-K, Item 7 MD&A)**

1. **Expenses fell, not revenue.** The 10-K states income from railway operations, net income and diluted EPS "increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily as a result of lower railway operating expenses," while "railway operating revenues were slightly lower" (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:84561). The reported railway operating ratio improved to 66.4% in 2024 from 76.5% in 2023 (chunk :84486) — a 10.1-point improvement, consistent with the operating-margin gain above.

2. **Absence of the 2023 Eastern Ohio incident costs.** 2023 included $1.1 billion of environmental and legal costs from the incident; 2024 had lower net incident expenses (chunks :102870 and :84561). This is the single largest identifiable swing factor.

3. **$433 million of gains on railway line sales** in 2024, which reduced net operating expenses (chunk :84561).

4. **Lower fuel prices, lower purchased-services costs and lower other expenses** (chunk :89477).

5. **Revenue was roughly flat to slightly down** (−0.3%), as "decreased fuel surcharge revenue, an adverse mix of traffic, and decreased pricing were nearly offset by increased volumes" (chunk :84561).

6. **Below the operating line, net margin lagged the operating-margin gain.** Management notes that "lower other income-net and higher interest expense on debt contributed to net income and diluted earnings per share that were only up slightly compared to the prior year" (chunk :89477). Pretax income tax expense rose from $493M to $707M (fact IDs 851009 and 851018), so the effective tax rate also increased.

**Caveats**
- The 10-K also presents non-GAAP adjusted figures: adjusted operating ratio was 65.8% in 2024 versus adjusted 67.4% in 2023 (chunk :89404), i.e. only a ~1.6-point improvement once the incident costs and line-sale gains are stripped out. The headline 10.1-point margin gain is therefore substantially non-recurring in nature; the underlying improvement is much smaller.
- The "only up slightly" language in the filing refers to adjusted net income/EPS; reported net income rose 43.5% because 2023 carried the $1.1 billion incident charge. I have not independently reconciled the adjusted net income figures.
- Margins are computed on total railway operating revenues; Norfolk Southern does not report a separate "gross margin," so operating and net margins are the appropriate profitability measures here.
